items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: if you hear “Take the A Train” and somebody says, “Why that’s Duke Ellington’s ‘Take the A Train.’”

ctx.x: Yeah, you just have to eat it in front of them and, “Boy, I wish you could share in this.”

Oh yeah. But encouraging young people to me is a privilege. Because a lot of these kids have no clue, like I said before. And I told them, I said my class is important but I’m more interested in your character and your integrity and your development as a person. If you do that that’s all I care about. In my jazz for listening class I said my goal for you is this: if you’re at a restaurant with your parents, and you hear “Take the A Train” and somebody says, “Why that’s Duke Ellington’s ‘Take the A Train.’” You…

an airport and you hear, “Oh boy that sounds like Professor Nelson’s Dad’s ‘Stolen Moments.” That’s what I’m looking for for those kids, to introduce them to the music and to keep that little flame going.
